newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delhaize cautious on European expansion.
newsitem.headline: Delhaize cautious on European expansion.

text.p: Belgian retailer Delhaize plans to consolidate its existing European branches before seeking new European markets.

Gui de Vaucleroy, chief executive of Delhaize, told Belgian financial daily L'Echo that Delhaize would expand into other European markets once they had obtained important market positions in existing locations.
"Today our strategy in Europe is clearly to improve (our) existing positions in Belgium, the north of France, Greece, and in the Czech Republic," he said in the interview.
In Greece Delhaize operates Alfa Beta Vassilopoulos, Delvita in the Czech Republic and P.G. in France.
"Our policy is that once the market and the partner is chosen, we focus on acquiring a significant piece of the market instead of small parts in different geographical territories".
Vaucleroy said Delhaize's Czech unit Delvita might enter the south of Poland, the south of Germany and the north of Austria.
He said a merger with a foreign retailer was not on the cards because "we do not see the necessity".
On the Belgian market he said he favoured more flexible opening hours and Sunday opening. "We are in favour of an enlargement in the possibilities of opening times."
He said Delhaize controlled between 13 to 14 percent of the Belgian market compared to a 8.5 percent share 10 years ago.
